diagnostic:
S2 icon rail delivered through the real driving port; both rail lanes fully green and the three unchanged-compatible consumer lanes still green. nav-collapse-icon-rail 17/17 scenarios, 106/106 steps (was 5 passed / 12 failed). nav-collapse-toggle 32/32, 207/207 (was 20 passed / 12 failed). navigation-bar 33/33, pwa-mobile-rendering 14/14, canzan-theme-system 28/28. check-arch PASSED, cargo fmt --check clean, xtask smoke "all gates green", release build of foundry-app clean. No oracle, support or feature-record file was edited; no test was added, weakened or skipped.

WHAT WAS BUILT. sidebar.html: each of the seven rail members (Home, Board, Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, Integrations, Instance admin, Sign out) gained one inline SVG with class sidebar__icon, aria-hidden=true, focusable=false and no title element, and its word moved into span.sidebar__label. Classes, hrefs, the sign-out form and the aria-current marking are unchanged; no aria-label was added anywhere, so the item's own text stays the one owner of the accessible name (D2, D3). Stylesheet: the collapsed region stops hiding the destinations - only sidebar__workspace and sidebar__identity keep display:none (D13) - every member becomes a 40px square target drawing a 20px glyph, the label is clipped with clip-path (never display:none, which would take the word out of the accessibility tree with it) and is revealed as a flyout on :hover and :focus-visible from one declaration (D4); the 480px arm lets both member groups wrap inside the bar and drops the flyout under its icon instead of to its right (D5, K14). The icon is display:none outside the collapsed geometry, so the expanded nav stays text only (K15). Every added rule names only --cz-* tokens; the glyph inherits the member's own text token through currentColor.

THE RENAME (D21). The stylesheet bytes changed, so foundry.4c73f62c.css became foundry.fb3aa227.css (sha256 fb3aa227590ded78ff5581cf1f1b562ea1f6107a572bd6fc709444fa7b31ced3) in the same change as the base.html href, the three cache-policy assertions in foundry-app/src/lib.rs, the VENDOR.md row and its note, and the CHANGELOG entry. The old name is left nowhere: grep for 4c73f62c over crates/ and CHANGELOG.md returns nothing, and check-arch's R2 and R3 layers confirm the name is its own sha256 prefix and the provenance row recomputes.

ICON PROVENANCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The path data is lucide-static 1.75.0 (ISC), npm tarball with its own sha256 recorded in VENDOR.md, retrieved 2026-11-18. The release tag is the one actually downloaded, not an invented one. The shape children of all seven upstream files were compared element-by-element against the inline markup and are identical in identical order; the note records the verification procedure, which icon name serves which destination, what was deliberately NOT copied from the upstream svg wrapper, and the ISC notice. No hashed row was added for the icons: an inline path in a template is not a served blob, so a row would be an integrity claim about a file that does not exist and R3 would fail looking for it (D2).

VENDOR.md:104 CORRECTION. The theme.js note said the gate "refuses those three attributes on every head script that paints stored state onto the document", which is not the criterion S1 shipped. It now states that the layer decides by what the asset NAMES in its comment-stripped source - a browser store and documentElement - that source cannot show WHEN it touches them so the test deliberately over-approximates and its refusal says so, and that its SECOND ARM requires defer on a head script whose asset does not name that pair. The note still makes no count claim.

CHANGELOG. One entry for the icon rail and the re-hash. In the same edit the nav-collapse-toggle entry above it lost the clause "while the nav is folded its items leave the keyboard order instead of hiding where the operator can still tab into them" and its own stale re-hash sentence: both ship in the same Unreleased section as the new entry and both are now false of the delivered rail, so leaving them would put two opposite claims in one release note.

REFACTORS: none taken. The S2 prefactoring - the move of NAV_PROBE and read_nav out of feature_nav_collapse.rs into crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/rail_reading.rs (D23) - was already done by the acceptance designer in a0123df, and the RED split at that commit (icon-rail 5 passed / 12 failed, toggle 20 passed / 12 failed) is the after-move-before-behaviour evidence; my first behaviour edit sits on top of it. No L1-L4 smell was found in the four production files this slice needed that a behaviour-preserving move would remove.

THRESHOLDS MET, NOT DODGED. The oracle's >= 8px icon floor is met by a 20x20 glyph; the >= 8px focused-label step up is met by a 1px clipped sliver growing into the shrink-to-fit flyout, read as a differential against the same label in the same page with the focus cleared. The clip-aware member visibility check (centre hit test resolving to the member or a descendant) passes on every member in both geometries, and the invisible-focusable set is empty in both.

UNRESOLVED INDEPENDENT FINDING, NOT MINE AND NOT A REGRESSION OF THIS REQUEST: cargo xtask ci exits 1 at `cargo deny check` - "advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok". The named advisory is a newly published RUSTSEC entry against lettre 0.11.22 (SMTP reply buffering, fixed in >= 0.11.24), and cargo deny additionally warns that deny.toml's ignore of RUSTSEC-2026-0381 no longer matches any crate. Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, deny.toml and every crate manifest are byte-unchanged by this slice, and lettre 0.11.22 is already at HEAD dfb6843, so this gate was red before the first edit; it is an advisory-clock finding owned by the host (dependency bump plus a deny.toml cleanup), raised here rather than repaired without authorisation. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVIDENCE, stated rather than hidden: deny runs before the acceptance stage, so the browser lanes did NOT run under xtask ci in that attempt. They were run individually instead, one single-tag release run per lane, which includes @needs-browser - that is the evidence above, and it covers every scenario of this feature's two lanes plus its three declared unchanged-compatible consumer lanes. The remainder of the ci suite that the deny failure cut short is NOT MEASURED by me; the host owns the recorded verification.
